title: 384-Well PCR Preparation Protocol
author: Opentrons
materials: Download your protocol and unzip if needed.

steps.title: Enter protocol parameters
steps.instruction: Enter the required parameters (number of samples, sample volume, number of mastermixes, mastermix volume, number of replicates per sample, and mastermix combination) and optionally a run ID for the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare mastermix tubes
steps.instruction: Pre‑mix each mastermix according to the experimental design and dispense the mixture into individual source tubes as illustrated.

steps.title: Plate mastermixes to columns
steps.instruction: Using a single‑channel pipette, transfer each mastermix from its source tube into the appropriate distribution columns of a 384‑well plate.

steps.title: Distribute mastermixes to plate
steps.instruction: Using an 8‑channel pipette, dispense the mastermix from the distribution columns into the designated wells of the final 384‑well plate.

steps.title: Download and unzip protocol
steps.instruction: Download the protocol package from the provided source and unzip the contents if they are compressed.

steps.title: Upload custom labware
steps.instruction: In the Opentrons App, navigate to More → Custom Labware → Add Labware and select the .json labware files to upload.

steps.title: Upload .py protocol file
steps.instruction: In the Opentrons App Protocol tab, upload the protocol script file with a .py extension.

steps.title: Arrange deck layout
steps.instruction: Place the required labware, tip racks, and pipettes on the robot deck according to the provided deck map.

steps.title: Calibrate labware and pipette
steps.instruction: Run the calibration routine in the Opentrons App to calibrate each piece of labware, the tip rack, and the pipette; consult the support articles for calibration tips if needed.

steps.title: Start protocol run
steps.instruction: Press the “Run” button in the Opentrons App. The robot will execute the protocol and write a .csv file containing sample traceability information to the robot’s Jupyter notebook server; the file name incorporates the optional run ID.
